title: Probabilistic cohort prober and resilience scheduler for gradual-rollout guards
author: Diana K. Alvarez
commits: 8c1d3f2 - introduce probabilistic cohort selection and core probing loop
b4a9e77 - add resilience scheduler with annealing-based throttle and budget accounting
f2e0a1d - telemetry hooks, metrics migration and unit tests
a5d9c88 - docs, examples and ci adjustments

description:
Motivation: We continue to see intermittent, low-amplitude latency regressions during gradual rollouts when small traffic cohorts interact with bursty load shapes. Current canary probes use uniform sampling and a single probe budget which results in either missed regressions on small cohorts or too aggressive probes that increase noise. This PR introduces a probabilistic cohort prober and a resilience scheduler that jointly allocate probe budget across cohort slices and adapt probe intensity based on short-term stability signals.

What this changes: Implements a cohort-aware prober that: 1) partitions traffic into probabilistic cohorts by request fingerprint and configurable slicing rules, 2) samples per-cohort probes with adjustable risk scores, and 3) emits structured probe telemetry for downstream canary evaluators. Adds a resilience scheduler that: 1) maintains a rolling budget ledger per-cohort, 2) uses an annealing-based throttle to reduce probe rate when regressions are suspected, and 3) exposes safety gates (latency delta and error ratio thresholds) to automatically pause probes or trigger reroute.

Design notes: The prober uses a configurable "seeded" RNG so runs can be reproduced in replay mode. Cohort scoring combines recent latency variance, request weight, and rollout stage to compute a probe utility. The scheduler applies an exponential backoff with decay and a small probabilistic allowance so that probes still sample the cohort at reduced rate (avoids blind spots). The ledger tracks both tokens (probe budget) and a cooldown credit to support bursty but limited probing.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for cohort selection, deterministic seeding, scheduler budget arithmetic, and a short integration test that runs a synthetic mixed workload (two cohorts with different qps and p95). Telemetry schema updated with probe events and shed reasons. CI workflow updated to include a lightweight perf-canary job that runs the integration test in the matrix. The branch initially had a flaky test (timing-sensitive) which was hardened by switching to time-mock injections; subsequent CI runs passed.

Operational impact and rollout: Default behavior is disabled (cockpit flag canary.prober.enabled=false). We will enable the prober behind a feature flag and run it in shadow mode for two weeks on a subset of customers. Observability added: per-cohort p50/p95, probe_rate, probe_success, probe_latency_delta, and probe.shed_reason. Runbook: if probe-induced noise exceeds threshold, ops can toggle canary.prober.mode=shadow | active | paused and adjust canary.scheduler.initial_budget.

Backward compatibility: No serving protocol changes. Metrics schema adds new optional fields. Configuration defaults tuned to be conservative.

Related work: ENG-1987 (continuous cohort-aware canary), PERF-402 (probe budget accounting), and internal doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1987/cohort-aware-prober (internal).

Release notes: Add probabilistic cohort prober and resilience scheduler (disabled by default). See docs/canary/probes.md for config and examples.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test added - [x] Telemetry schema updated - [x] Docs and example config - [x] Feature-flagged and safe defaults

release_notes: Introduces probabilistic cohort prober and resilience scheduler to improve canary sensitivity while limiting noise. Feature is disabled by default and gated behind canary.prober.enabled. Add per-cohort telemetry and a mixed-workload example.
notes: Follow-up: add an A/B evaluation comparing uniform probes vs probabilistic cohorts on production traffic; consider integrating with rollout controller to automatically adjust canary weights based on probe signals.
